title: Introduction to spconform
text: spconform provides distribution-free, finite-sample prediction intervals spatial spatio-temporal data relaxing exchangeability assumption standard conformal prediction. offers two core procedures: scp_geostatistical() point-referenced (geostatistical) data, using locally weighted split conformal prediction spatial (, optionally, temporal) Gaussian kernels. scp_areal() areal (lattice) data, using neighbourhood-weighted leave-one-conformal procedure based graph adjacency structure. procedures model-agnostic: supply point predictor (linear model, GAM, random forest, kriging, anything else), spconform handles conformal calibration layer, producing prediction intervals guaranteed marginal coverage level regardless whether predictor well specified. vignette illustrates procedures meuse river dataset (Pebesma Bivand 2005), standard geostatistics benchmark distributed sp package. use log-transformed zinc concentration (ppm) response, projected coordinates spatial index. 155 sampling locations trace diagonal band following natural course river.
code: library(sp) data(meuse)  s <- as.matrix(meuse[, c("x", "y")]) y <- log(meuse$zinc) plot(meuse$x, meuse$y, col = rgb(0.2, 0.4, 0.8, 0.5), pch = 19,      xlab = "X coordinate", ylab = "Y coordinate",      main = "Meuse Sampling Locations")

title: Introduction to spconform
text: scp_geostatistical() requires pred_fun signature function(s_train, y_train, s_new), returning point predictions new locations s_new. use deliberately simple quadratic trend surface, fit ordinary least squares: predictor intentionally simple; point conformal prediction resulting intervals remain valid even underlying model imperfect.
code: pred_fun <- function(s_train, y_train, s_new) {   fit <- lm(y_train ~ s_train[, 1] + s_train[, 2] +               I(s_train[, 1]^2) + I(s_train[, 2]^2))   cbind(1, s_new[, 1], s_new[, 2], s_new[, 1]^2, s_new[, 2]^2) %*% coef(fit) }

title: Introduction to spconform
text: split data 70/30 training test sets, construct 90% prediction intervals test locations: coverage_report() compares intervals (, known) true test values:
code: set.seed(1) n <- nrow(s) idx <- sample(n, floor(0.7 * n))  s_train <- s[idx, ]; y_train <- y[idx] s_test  <- s[-idx, ]; y_test  <- y[-idx]  out <- scp_geostatistical(s_train, y_train, s_test, pred_fun,                            alpha = 0.1, seed = 1) print(out) #> <spconform> geostatistical conformal prediction #> Target coverage: 90.0% #> Number of prediction points: 47 #>    pred lower upper #> 1 6.573 5.661 7.484 #> 2 6.255 5.344 7.167 #> 3 5.954 5.043 6.866 #> 4 6.455 5.544 7.367 #> 5 6.171 5.260 7.083 #> 6 5.773 4.862 6.685 #> ... (41 more) coverage_report(out, y_test) #> $coverage #> [1] 0.9574468 #>  #> $mean_width #> [1] 2.210471

title: Introduction to spconform
text: plot() method displays point predictions, intervals, (optionally) true values:
code: plot(out, y_true = y_test)

what: Assessing stability via Monte Carlo replication
title: Introduction to spconform
text: single train/test split can misleading. repeat split 50 times assess whether coverage stable around nominal target:  mean coverage across replications close nominal 90% target, low variability across data partitions — indicating coverage guarantee stable artifact single split.
code: set.seed(123) coverages <- numeric(50) widths    <- numeric(50)  for (i in 1:50) {   idx_i <- sample(n, floor(0.7 * n))   s_tr <- s[idx_i, ]; y_tr <- y[idx_i]   s_te <- s[-idx_i, ]; y_te <- y[-idx_i]    out_i <- scp_geostatistical(s_tr, y_tr, s_te, pred_fun,                                alpha = 0.1, seed = i)    rep_i <- coverage_report(out_i, y_te)   coverages[i] <- rep_i$coverage   widths[i]    <- rep_i$mean_width }  mean(coverages) #> [1] 0.9204255 sd(coverages) #> [1] 0.04358497 mean(widths) #> [1] 1.973462 hist(coverages, breaks = 15, col = "lightblue", border = "white",      main = "Empirical Coverage Across 50 Random Splits",      xlab = "Empirical Coverage", xlim = c(0.7, 1)) abline(v = 0.90, col = "red", lwd = 2, lty = 2) legend("topleft", legend = "Nominal target (0.90)",        col = "red", lty = 2, bty = "n")

title: Introduction to spconform
text: scp_geostatistical() weights calibration points proximity target location, interval width can vary spatially, reflecting local data density configuration:
code: plot_df <- data.frame(   x = s_test[, 1],   y = s_test[, 2],   width = out$upper - out$lower )  plot(plot_df$x, plot_df$y,      cex = plot_df$width, pch = 19,      col = rgb(0.2, 0.4, 0.8, 0.5),      xlab = "X coordinate", ylab = "Y coordinate",      main = "Spatial Distribution of Interval Width")

title: Introduction to spconform
text: scp_areal() targets data observed fixed set areal units (e.g. counties, grid cells) linked adjacency structure, rather continuous coordinates. illustrate phenomenon, aggregate point-referenced Meuse data onto regular 6×66\times6 grid, retaining occupied cells taking mean log-zinc concentration within areal response. adj binary adjacency matrix linking grid-adjacent cells. now apply scp_areal() nominal 80% coverage level, using default neighbourhood-mean predictor:  areal units show narrow intervals, occasional exceptions units sparse neighbourhood (e.g., boundary cells grid). desirable property scp_areal(): units fewer graph neighbours smaller, less informative local calibration set, wider interval correctly reflects higher predictive uncertainty periphery spatial domain, rather understating .
code: xbreaks <- seq(min(meuse$x), max(meuse$x), length.out = 7) ybreaks <- seq(min(meuse$y), max(meuse$y), length.out = 7)  meuse$cell_x  <- cut(meuse$x, xbreaks, include.lowest = TRUE, labels = FALSE) meuse$cell_y  <- cut(meuse$y, ybreaks, include.lowest = TRUE, labels = FALSE) meuse$cell_id <- (meuse$cell_y - 1) * 6 + meuse$cell_x  agg <- aggregate(log(zinc) ~ cell_id, data = meuse, FUN = mean) names(agg) <- c("cell_id", "y")  cell_coords <- unique(meuse[, c("cell_id", "cell_x", "cell_y")]) agg <- merge(agg, cell_coords, by = "cell_id") agg <- agg[order(agg$cell_id), ]  n_cells <- nrow(agg) adj <- matrix(0, n_cells, n_cells) for (i in 1:n_cells) {   for (j in 1:n_cells) {     if (i != j) {       dx <- abs(agg$cell_x[i] - agg$cell_x[j])       dy <- abs(agg$cell_y[i] - agg$cell_y[j])       if (dx <= 1 && dy <= 1) adj[i, j] <- 1     }   } } out2 <- scp_areal(agg$y, adjacency = adj, alpha = 0.2) print(out2) #> <spconform> areal conformal prediction #> Target coverage: 80.0% #> Number of prediction points: 21 #>    pred lower upper #> 1 5.966 5.148 6.785 #> 2 5.749 4.854 6.643 #> 3 5.981 5.145 6.817 #> 4 5.502 4.608 6.396 #> 5 6.495 4.576 8.415 #> 6 5.934 5.116 6.752 #> ... (15 more) summary(out2) #> spconform summary #> ------------------ #> Type:               areal  #> Target coverage:    80.0%  #> Mean interval width: 1.8666  #> Median interval width: 1.7888 coverage_report(out2, agg$y) #> $coverage #> [1] 0.7619048 #>  #> $mean_width #> [1] 1.866613 plot(out2, y_true = agg$y)

title: Conformal Prediction for Spatially and Spatio-Temporally Dependent Data
text: Standard conformal prediction assumes exchangeable data — assumption routinely violated spatial settings nearby observations similar distant ones. Existing R packages address either purely temporal dependence (conformalForecast, AdaptiveConformal) ..d./exchangeable data (conformalInference, conformalClassification, cfcausal), none provides documented, unit-tested, unified solution spatial data CRAN. spconform , knowledge, first R package offer conformal prediction spanning major spatial data structures optional spatio-temporal extension. > Status: spconform passed R CMD check ---cran 0 errors, > 0 warnings, 0 notes Windows 11 (R 4.6.1), win-builder (R-devel), > R-hub v2 (Linux, Windows, macOS, donttest). package CRAN-ready > submitted CRAN soon submission form re-opens. > permanent, citable snapshot version 0.1.0 archived Zenodo > (DOI ). accompanying manuscript currently preparation > submission Journal Statistical Software.

code: library(spconform) library(sp)  data(meuse) s <- as.matrix(meuse[, c("x", "y")]) y <- log(meuse$zinc)  # Any user-supplied point predictor pred_fun <- function(s_train, y_train, s_new) {   fit <- lm(y_train ~ s_train[, 1] + s_train[, 2] +             I(s_train[, 1]^2) + I(s_train[, 2]^2))   cbind(1, s_new[, 1], s_new[, 2],         s_new[, 1]^2, s_new[, 2]^2) %*% coef(fit) }  # 90% locally weighted conformal intervals set.seed(123) idx <- sample(nrow(s), floor(0.7 * nrow(s))) out <- scp_geostatistical(s[idx, ], y[idx], s[-idx, ], pred_fun, alpha = 0.1)  print(out) #> <spconform> geostatistical conformal prediction #> Target coverage: 90.0% #> Number of prediction points: 47  coverage_report(out, y[-idx]) #> $coverage #> [1] 0.957 #> $mean_width #> [1] 2.21

code: # Aggregate Meuse to a 6x6 grid (21 occupied cells) xbreaks <- seq(min(meuse$x), max(meuse$x), length.out = 7) ybreaks <- seq(min(meuse$y), max(meuse$y), length.out = 7) meuse$cell_x  <- cut(meuse$x, xbreaks, include.lowest = TRUE, labels = FALSE) meuse$cell_y  <- cut(meuse$y, ybreaks, include.lowest = TRUE, labels = FALSE) meuse$cell_id <- (meuse$cell_y - 1) * 6 + meuse$cell_x  agg <- aggregate(log(zinc) ~ cell_id, data = meuse, FUN = mean) names(agg) <- c("cell_id", "y") cell_coords <- unique(meuse[, c("cell_id", "cell_x", "cell_y")]) agg <- merge(agg, cell_coords, by = "cell_id") agg <- agg[order(agg$cell_id), ]  # Build adjacency matrix (Queen contiguity) n_cells <- nrow(agg) adj <- matrix(0, n_cells, n_cells) for (i in 1:n_cells) {   for (j in 1:n_cells) {     if (i != j) {       dx <- abs(agg$cell_x[i] - agg$cell_x[j])       dy <- abs(agg$cell_y[i] - agg$cell_y[j])       if (dx <= 1 && dy <= 1) adj[i, j] <- 1     }   } }  # 80% neighbourhood-weighted conformal intervals out_areal <- scp_areal(agg$y, adjacency = adj, alpha = 0.2, decay = 0.5) coverage_report(out_areal, agg$y) #> $coverage #> [1] 0.81 #> $mean_width #> [1] 1.79

code: library(mgcv) library(bmstdr)  data("nysptime") df <- nysptime[complete.cases(nysptime[, c("utmx", "utmy", "y8hrmax", "Day", "Month")]), ] df$day_idx <- ifelse(df$Month == 7, df$Day, 31 + df$Day)  s <- as.matrix(df[, c("utmx", "utmy")]) t <- df$day_idx s_3d <- cbind(s, t) y <- df$y8hrmax  # Spatio-temporal GAM predictor pred_fun_st <- function(s_train, y_train, s_new) {   train_df <- data.frame(x = s_train[, 1], y = s_train[, 2],                          day = s_train[, 3], z = y_train)   fit <- gam(z ~ te(x, y, day, k = c(8, 8, 4)), data = train_df)   new_df <- data.frame(x = s_new[, 1], y = s_new[, 2], day = s_new[, 3])   as.numeric(predict(fit, newdata = new_df)) }  set.seed(123) n <- nrow(s_3d) train_idx <- sample(n, floor(0.7 * n)) out_st <- scp_geostatistical(   s_train = s_3d[train_idx, ],   y_train = y[train_idx],   s0 = s_3d[-train_idx, ],   pred_fun = pred_fun_st,   t_train = t[train_idx],   t0 = t[-train_idx],   temporal_bandwidth = 5,   alpha = 0.1,   split = 0.5 )  coverage_report(out_st, y[-train_idx]) #> $coverage #> [1] 0.909 #> $mean_width #> [1] 41.7

title: Neighbourhood-Weighted Conformal Prediction for Areal (Lattice) Data — scp_areal
